healthReform.source: Journal of the European Economic Association

healthReform.title: Life-Cycle Wages and Human Capital Investments: Selection and Missing Data
healthReform.abstract: AbstractWe derive wage equations with individual-specific coefficients from a structural model of human capital investment over the life-cycle. This model allows for interruptions in labour market participation and deals with missing data and attrition problems. We propose a new framework that deals with missingness at random and is based on factor decompositions that allow for flexible control of selection. Our approach leads to an interactive effect wage specification, which we estimate using long administrative panel data on male wages in the private sector in France. A structural function

healthReform.title: Diversification, Market Entry, and the Global Internet Backbone
healthReform.abstract: AbstractIn many industries, buyers diversify their supplier base to manage supplier disruption risk. We investigate the importance of such diversification as a determinant of demand and supplier entry in the context of the internet backbone, the worldwide network of undersea fibre-optic cables that underpins the internet. We specify a model of international bandwidth demand and cable operators’ dynamic entry and supply choices. healthReform.title: Optimal Climate Policy with Demographic Transitions
healthReform.abstract: AbstractThis paper develops a framework to integrate demographic change into climate policy analysis. We build an overlapping-generations climate-economy model with a rich demographic structure, allowing population growth and survival probabilities to vary over time. These features endogenously determine the age composition of society and shape aggregate preferences. healthReform.title: Interest-Based Negotiation over Natural Resources: Experimental Evidence from Liberia
healthReform.abstract: AbstractWe experimentally evaluate whether an interest-based negotiation training for community leaders in Liberia improves their ability to strike beneficial deals related to their land and forests. We use environmental assessments, lab-in-the-field, and surveys and find that trainees are 27% more likely to reach a beneficial agreement, and it raises the total surplus earned by $2.74 USD, which is a 42% increase. healthReform.source: Journal of the European Economic Association

healthReform.title: Fiscal Rules, Austerity in Public Administration, and Political Accountability: Evidence from a Natural Experiment in Colombia
healthReform.abstract: AbstractFiscal rules are a popular tool to improve fiscal discipline and reduce waste in public spending, but their effectiveness and political feasibility remain unclear, particularly in weakly institutionalized settings. We leverage exogenous variation across Colombian municipalities in exposure to a fiscal rule that limits the operating expenditures of local governments. Our difference-in-differences analysis yields three main findings. First, the fiscal rule effectively reduces operating expenditures and the probability of a current deficit. healthReform.source: Journal of the European Economic Association

healthReform.title: Dodging Day Zero: Drought, Adaptation, and Inequality in Cape Town
healthReform.abstract: AbstractA near-catastrophic drought in Cape Town, South Africa, illustrates three implications of climate change for publicly provided utility services. First, to reduce aggregate water demand, the public utility increased prices, leading to large demand reductions by richer households. Prior to the drought, they used twice the public piped water of poorer households. At the peak of the drought, they use less. Second, some of the differential demand reduction comes from richer households substituting away from public water toward privately financed groundwater. This private adaptation both low
healthReform.source: Journal of the European Economic Association

healthReform.title: When Broadband Comes to Banks: Credit Supply, Market Structure, and Information Acquisition
healthReform.abstract: AbstractThis paper studies how broadband internet affects bank credit supply to non-financial firms. We rely on loan-level data from the Italian Credit Register and quasi-experimental variation in the diffusion of broadband. Our estimates include firm-time fixed effects to control for the effect of broadband on firm demand. We find that branches in municipalities reached by fast internet increase loan supply and reduce interest rates. healthReform.source: Journal of the European Economic Association

healthReform.title: “Immigration, Search and Redistribution: A Quantitative Assessment of Native Welfare:” Comment
healthReform.abstract: AbstractIn “Immigration, search and redistribution: A quantitative assessment of native welfare,” a paper by Battisti et al. published in the August 2018 issue of the Journal of the European Economic Association, the authors inquire about how migration to 20 Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) countries affects the welfare of the countries’ native workers. In this comment, we raise several concerns regarding the analytical and the empirical parts of the Battisti et al.’s inquiry that bear on this effect. healthReform.title: On the Geographic Implications of Carbon Taxes
healthReform.abstract: AbstractUsing a multi-sector dynamic spatial integrated assessment model, we argue that a carbon tax introduced by the European Union and rebated locally can, if not too large, increase the size of Europe’s economy by concentrating economic activity in its high-productivity non-agricultural core and by incentivising immigration to the European Union. The resulting change in the spatial distribution of economic activity improves global efficiency and welfare. A carbon tax introduced by the United States generates similar effects. healthReform.title: Presidential Address: Neighborhood Effects and Missing Markets for Opportunity
healthReform.abstract: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3197-3222 Abstract Experimental and quasi-experimental studies show that childhood neighborhoods have substantial causal impacts on children's adult earnings and other long-term socioeconomic outcomes. Several market failures are likely to lead to excessive residential segregation by parental income and to an undersupply of mixed-income neighborhoods. Missing markets for opportunity originate in capital market imperfections for borrowing on children's future earnings, neighbor spillovers, behavioral biases, and housing search frictions. healthReform.title: Contextually Private Mechanisms
healthReform.abstract: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3223-3262 Abstract A designer employs a dynamic protocol to elicit private information. Protocols produce a set of contextual privacy violations—information learned that may be superfluous given the context. A protocol is maximally contextually private if there is no protocol that produces a proper subset of the violations it produces, while implementing the choice rule. healthReform.title: Manipulation-Robust Prediction
healthReform.abstract: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3263-3293 Abstract An increasing number of decisions are guided by machine learning algorithms. But when consequential decisions are encoded in algorithms, individuals may strategically alter their behavior to achieve desired outcomes. This paper develops an empirical approach that adjusts decision algorithms to anticipate manipulation. By explicitly modeling incentives to manipulate, our approach produces decision rules that are stable under manipulation, even when the rules are fully transparent. We stress-test this approach through a large field experiment

healthReform.title: Risk-Sharing Tests and Covariate Shocks: Drought, Floods, and Pests in Uganda
healthReform.abstract: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3294-3329 Abstract Efficient risk sharing implies a simple factor structure for marginal utilities of expenditure (MUEs): Pareto weights divided by a common price. The standard approach infers MUEs from total expenditures, implicitly assuming homothetic preferences, unitary income elasticities, and identical price elasticities. healthReform.title: Optimal Public Transportation Networks: Evidence from the World's Largest Bus Rapid Transit System in Jakarta
healthReform.abstract: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3330-3379 Abstract Designing public transport networks involves trade-offs between coverage, service frequency, and direct service. We use the expansion of the bus system in Jakarta, Indonesia, to study these trade-offs. We analyze how new direct connections, changes in bus travel time, and wait-time reductions affect bus ridership and aggregate flows and estimate a transit network demand model by matching the route launch events. healthReform.title: Corporate Tax Cuts, Firm Growth, and Workers' Earnings
healthReform.abstract: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3380-3422 Abstract We study the effects of the largest corporate income tax cut in US history on firms and workers. To identify causal effects, we use employer-employee matched tax records and event studies comparing similarly sized firms in the same industry that faced divergent tax changes due to their preexisting legal status. Tax cuts cause increases in firms' investment, sales, profits, employment, and payrolls, with earnings gains concentrated among highly paid workers. healthReform.title: Marriage, Fertility, and Cultural Integration in Italy
healthReform.abstract: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3423-3463 Abstract We study cultural integration as an equilibrium outcome of marital matching along cultural and education lines and intrahousehold investment decisions regarding fertility and cultural socialization. Our model allows us to identify cultural-ethnic-group-specific investment parameters and spousal preferences for marital matching. healthReform.title: Defying Distance? The Provision of Medical Services in the Digital Age
healthReform.abstract: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3464-3509 Abstract Digital platforms reduce geographic frictions, enabling better matching between service providers and users. I quantify reallocation gains in Swedish online health care, using nationwide time-conditional random assignment between patients and physicians. Matching high-risk patients with doctors effective at reducing Emergency Room visits lowers such visits by 4.4 percent (SE 1.3); reallocations also reduce Counter-Guideline antibiotics by 3.1 percent (1.4). healthReform.title: The Environmental Bias of Corporate Income Taxation
healthReform.abstract: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3510-3551 Abstract We study the relationship between corporate income taxation and carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions in the United States. We show CO2-intensive firms benefit more from the tax advantage of debt and pay lower income taxes on their capital income. Building on these new facts, we provide evidence that a cut in the corporate income tax rate leads to a larger expansion of clean firms. healthReform.title: Rationing by Race
healthReform.abstract: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3552-3585 Abstract We document how deepening resource scarcity results in rationing on the basis of race in a high-stakes setting: health care. Using detailed, time stamped data on 107,000 inpatient admissions to a large health system, we find that in-hospital mortality increases for Black but not White patients as hospitals reach capacity. healthReform.abstract: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3586-3621 Abstract We provide experimental evidence on the intergenerational impacts of secondary education subsidies in a low-income context, leveraging a randomized controlled trial and 15-year longitudinal follow-up. Secondary school scholarships delay fertility, reduce unwanted pregnancies, and change partner selection. Under-one mortality is reduced by half. agingHealth.abstract: 当前，县域医共体的治理困境既包含权力配置失衡引发的体制性障碍，也存在服务协同不足、资源错配、医保激励不足、数智技术应用滞后等机制性问题；基于“控制钮框架”理论，以权力、服务、资源、利益、技术为“控制钮”，为破解县域医共体治理难题、优化体制机制提供了新的思路——以权力结构的契约化重塑为核心，撬动服务模式向健康本位转型，驱动健康资源精准高效配置，并通过医保战略性购买与数智技术赋能，构建激励相容的治理生...

agingHealth.title: 县域医共体支付机制重构的国际经验及启示
agingHealth.abstract: 当前，我国县域医共体建设已从组织整合和资源下沉阶段进入机制完善和功能提升阶段，如何推动服务体系从“以疾病治疗为中心”转向“以健康为中心”，已成为亟须明确的重要问题。在此过程中，县域医共体支付面临现实困境：基层健康责任缺乏有效支付、多元资金缺乏统筹、县乡利益联动不足、绩效考核偏重过程指标，等等。对此，可借鉴英国、美国、澳大利亚的基层健康管理机制建设经验，探索购买基层承担的居民健康责任，构建健康责任购...

agingHealth.abstract: 农旅融合已成为促进乡村振兴、助推共同富裕的重要新业态。为评估农旅融合的共同富裕效应及其作用机制，本文基于县级面板数据，以全国休闲农业与乡村旅游示范县政策作为外生冲击，采用多时点DID方法评估农旅融合对县域共同富裕的影响。其次，基于中国家庭追踪调查数据，从微观层面拓展分析农旅融合对人群差距的影响。研究发现农旅融合显著提升县域共同富裕水平，该效应在资本禀赋和产业基础较好地区更显著，且主要通过增加固定资...

agingHealth.title: 基于函数型主成分分析的时空数据可分性研究
agingHealth.abstract: 现代科技的发展使得时空数据日益丰富，而传统的可分性假设在应对复杂的时空过程时面临极大限制。本文基于函数型数据分析的方法提出了对于非平稳时空数据的弱可分模型，通过将数据分解为一系列空间相关随机场和时变特征函数，建立了更为灵活且简洁的时空协方差结构。针对所关注的时空数据类型，本文提出了基于边际协方差的函数型主成分估计，并利用该估计量进一步建立了弱可分性的统计检验及渐近性质。区别于已有检验方法，本文提出...

agingHealth.title: 中介效应的估计与应用——基于高维线性潜在混淆变量模型
agingHealth.abstract: 中介效应被广泛应用于探讨经济变量之间的因果关系及其作用机制。现有学者大多基于线性结构方程模型使用最小二乘法对中介效应进行估计，但模型中可能包含不可观测的遗漏变量会导致有偏的系数估计，进而会降低中介效应的因果解释力度。为此，本文首先探讨Imai等（2010）和Huber等（2020）提出的因果中介效应非参数识别方法，并分析该方法与线性结构方程模型参数估计的等价条件。进而，本文探讨在线性结构方程模型中...

agingHealth.abstract: 为深入探讨残障统计领域的最新进展与未来趋势，应对残障数据采集、整合与分析中日益复杂的挑战，推动统计方法的创新与应用拓展，同时促进统计学与管理学、人工智能、数据科学等学科的交叉融合，深化交流合作，培养高素质复合型人才，以更好服务于残疾人事业高质量发展与社会治理现代化等国家重大需求，第十一届残疾人数据科学研讨会暨2026中国统计学会残障统计分会年会拟定于2026年11月召开。本次会议...

agingHealth.title: 丰富统计理论新知识  了解经济社会新动向  欢迎订阅2027年度《统计研究》
agingHealth.abstract: 《统计研究》是由国家统计局主管，中国统计学会、国家统计局统计科学研究所主办的学术刊物，国内外公开发行。自1984年创刊以来，在广大作者、读者的关心支持下，逐渐形成了自己的办刊特色，成为统计领域最具权威性和影响力的学术刊物。多年来，《统计研究》作为“交流科研成果，繁荣学术研究，创新理论知识，推动实际工作”的窗口，助力中国哲学社会科学统计学科自主知识体系建设，积极推动中国特色统计理论...

agingHealth.title: 本期导读
agingHealth.abstract: 《数字经济下居民真实生活成本指数构建与应用——基于超越GDP视角的研究》一文以超越GDP为核心视角,立足居民福利一生活成本框架,将住户无酬服务和“免费”产品纳入测算,构建我国城镇居民真实生活成本指数。研究发现,纳入住户无酬服务的综合商品与“免费”产品在提升消费者效用水平上的作用大致相当;两者纳入测算后,城镇居民环比真实生活成本指数(CPIT5)较传统CPI年均提高约1.1个百分点...

agingHealth.title: 我国人口发展趋势及政策启示
agingHealth.abstract: 人口负增长、少子化和老龄化给我国人口安全、经济发展和社会保障等各方面带来了挑战和风险。本文在传统队列要素法高、中、低方案确定性参数设定的基础上，基于“充分覆盖”的想法，提出一种针对总和生育率不确定性的稳健估计方法，并结合队列要素法，在高、中、低三种总和生育率水平下，对我国2026—2100年人口趋势进行预测并给出置信区间。研究发现，未来我国人口总量将持续下降，少子化和老龄化程度将进一步加深。短期而...

agingHealth.title: 政府行为对违约债券回收的影响
agingHealth.abstract: 激活长期沉淀的零回收债券对化解债券市场风险极为重要，而坚持市场化是违约债券回收的基本原则。本文基于2014—2024年的违约债券回收数据，实证分析了政府行为对违约债券启动及完成回收的影响及其作用机制。在对Logistic回归模型中调节效应的判别方法进行补充后，本文基于该判别方法及再中心化方法量化研究了产能利用率等因素的调节作用。研究结果表明，减少政府过度干预可促进违约债券启动并完成回收；降低信息不...

agingHealth.title: 中国儿童居住安排变迁及其对家庭照护的启示
agingHealth.abstract: 在人口流动背景下，儿童居住安排的变化关系着家庭照护模式的调整以及儿童发展质量。文章基于2000、2010和2020年全国人口普查微观数据，系统考察21世纪以来中国儿童与父母、祖父母同住模式的变化趋势及其城乡和年龄别差异。研究发现：（1）中国儿童与父母双方共同居住的比例快速下降；（2）儿童与父母居住分离的原因由“留守”主导向儿童独自流动、单亲、留守等多因素演进；（3）不同发展阶段儿童家庭亲子居住分离...

agingHealth.title: 婚姻教育匹配的生育效应研究——基于“孩次递进”分析框架的实证发现
agingHealth.abstract: 婚姻关系中，教育匹配特征作为家庭结构的重要维度，对夫妻生育决策具有深刻影响。文章基于中国家庭追踪调查（CFPS）2010～2022年数据，通过构建“孩次递进”分析框架，运用泊松回归与事件史分析方法系统考察了婚姻教育匹配对家庭生育行为的影响。研究发现，从终身生育数量来看，教育同质婚夫妇的教育水平与生育行为呈显著的负相关关系，教育水平越高，生育数量越低；在教育异质婚中，丈夫受教育程度比妻子高两级及以上...

agingHealth.title: 技能培训券的稳就业效应——以“投资于人”为视角
agingHealth.abstract: 通过技能培训提高劳动者的技能水平、缓解结构性就业矛盾，对于推进投资于人的发展具有重要意义。文章以职业技能电子培训券政策为研究对象，实证检验其就业效应，并从投资于人的视角探讨其具体作用路径。研究发现，技能培训券政策的实施显著提升了地区在岗职工人数，改善了地区的整体就业状况。机制分析表明，技能培训券政策通过带动政府增加社会保障与就业支出、对企业的就业补贴，能够显著改善地区整体就业状况。在个人层面，技能...

agingHealth.title: 就业质量类型的识别及心理健康效应研究
agingHealth.abstract: 在就业形态日益多元化背景下，识别多维就业质量的类型分化及其心理健康效应具有重要意义。文章利用中国家庭追踪调查（CFPS）数据，从工作时间、经济报酬和制度保障3个维度选取6项指标，采用潜类别分析方法识别劳动者的就业质量类型，并检验不同就业质量类型对心理健康的差异化影响。研究发现，当前劳动力市场中劳动者的就业质量呈现四种差异化类型，占比从高到低依次为：以长工时、低收入、低保障为特征的“非稳定型”；以长...

agingHealth.title: 适老化改造的健康红利与照料减负——基于“厕所革命”的实证研究
agingHealth.abstract: 在人口老龄化持续加深与“投资于人”发展导向不断强化的背景下，文章将“厕所革命”重新定位为一种潜在的老年健康干预措施，实证检验其对缓解农村老年人失能风险和家庭照料负担的影响。基于中国健康与养老追踪调查（CHARLS）2011～2020年的面板数据，运用交叠双重差分模型，文章分析了旱厕改造为冲水厕所对降低老年群体失能风险的因果效应。结果表明，改厕显著降低了老年人的失能风险：如厕困难比例平均下降15.6...

agingHealth.title: 总量不足还是结构错位：中国农村老年人养老服务供需状况研究
agingHealth.abstract: 准确识别养老服务需求是优化供给结构、破解资源错配的前提。文章采用四种方案预测农村老年人的健康状态，评估其养老服务需求并进行供需匹配分析。研究发现，农村养老服务体系的核心矛盾是设施导向供给与项目导向需求的结构性错位。基准方案的结果显示，2030年，农村老年人口将达到16 202万人，中度及以上失能人口超2 000万人。家庭养老仍居核心地位，而完全依赖机构和社区养老的老年人规模有限，仅200万人左右。...

agingHealth.title: 以养节医：居家和社区养老服务对城镇老年居民医疗负担的影响
agingHealth.abstract: 在人口老龄化持续深化与医疗费用不断攀升的背景下，着眼于“在地安老”的居家和社区养老服务能否减轻城镇老年居民医疗负担、实现“以养节医”，具有重要研究价值。文章以居家和社区养老服务改革试点政策为准自然实验，基于2011～2020年中国健康与养老追踪调查数据，使用渐进双重差分法实证评估居家和社区养老服务对城镇老年居民医疗负担的影响。研究发现，居家和社区养老服务改革试点显著减轻了城镇老年居民的医疗负担，表...

agingHealth.abstract: 在人口老龄化的背景下，建立符合中国人口特征及发展规律的死亡率预测模型，对中国人口预测、长寿风险度量和长寿风险管理具有重要意义。文章通过构建自适应Lee-Carter因子模型，将人均受教育年限、人均可支配收入和人均医疗保险基金支出纳入Lee-Carter模型，直接拟合了经济变迁等因素带来的模型参数结构性时变问题，提高了模型的样本外推预测能力，为人口研究和长寿风险度量提供了有效工具。实证结果表明，（1...

agingHealth.abstract: 双重差分模型广泛应用于经济政策评估与分析。在此模型框架下，政策评估者通常采用逆概率加权法估计政策干预组的平均处理效应（Average Treatment Effect on the Treated,ATT）。现有研究的不足在于大多采用参数或非参数方法估计倾向得分函数，导致平衡权重估计量容易出现极端值，进而使得ATT估计量不稳定且精度较低。同时，现有方法难以有效消除处理组与控制组协变量不平衡对ATT...

agingHealth.title: 不确定视角下融合历史与当前极差信息的波动率模型建模与应用
agingHealth.abstract: 为探索金融投资者实现风险高效控制和收益最大化等问题，本文在不确定视角下提出了实时随机异质性条件自回归极差（RT–CARR）模型。基于此模型，推导得出极差的条件分布、条件k阶矩、条件峰度、样本外向前多步的波动率估计以及严平稳条件，运用拟极大似然估计法得到该模型的参数估计，并数值模拟验证了估计的有效性。将RT–CARR模型应用于股票指数数据，基于样本内数据的拟合结果表明，实时信息对当前波动率具有显著影...

agingHealth.abstract: 本文借鉴熊彼特增长模型，构建同时考虑金融深化和广化的经济增长模型，研究本地区和经济关联地区金融深化和广化通过不同科技创新模式对本地区实体经济发展的影响机理，并基于2013—2024年我国31个省份样本数据，对理论模型结果进行实证检验。研究发现，实体经济发展存在显著的正向空间溢出效应；本地区和经济关联地区的金融深化都将促进本地区实体经济发展，本地区金融广化对自身实体经济发展的影响不显著，经济关联地区...

agingHealth.title: 电子渠道业务能够抑制银行流动性囤积吗？——基于银行开设电子银行的准自然实验
agingHealth.abstract: 在数字化变革的浪潮下，电子渠道业务的发展为银行流动性管理带来了新的机遇与挑战，也为探究其如何影响流动性囤积行为提供了重要契机。本文基于2007—2024年我国商业银行的微观数据，考察了银行开展电子渠道业务对流动性囤积的影响及其内在机理。研究发现，银行开设网上银行、手机银行和微信银行均能有效抑制流动性囤积，且网上银行凭借便捷性对流动性囤积的抑制效果最大。电子渠道业务通过线上交易结算加速了流动性运转，...

agingHealth.abstract: 提高财政支出对产出的乘数效应，是积极财政政策提质增效的应有之意。本文基于我国省际层面面板数据，使用局部投影技术实证研究财政支出乘数对人口年龄结构的状态相依性。研究结果表明，不论是从单期效应还是累积效应看，高老龄化状态下的财政支出乘数都远远小于低老龄化状态下的财政支出乘数。此外，人口老龄化对投资尤其是私人投资的抑制作用将会削弱财政支出的有效性。进一步将局部投影技术与Blinder-Oaxaca分解相...

agingHealth.abstract: 长期护理保险在保障亲代失能老年人身心健康的同时能否提升子代家庭消费，对扩大内需乃至畅通国内经济循环具有重要意义。文章采用2012～2022年中国家庭追踪调查数据，运用多期双重差分方法，检验长期护理保险对家庭消费影响的代际传递效应。研究发现，亲代参加长期护理保险能够显著提高子代家庭消费，且该结果通过了平行趋势检验和一系列稳健性检验。在影响机制上，亲代参加长期护理保险有助于减轻试点城市子代家庭的代际支...

agingHealth.abstract: 随着中国人口老龄化进程的加快，构建老年友好社区成为提升老年人生活质量和促进银发经济发展的重要举措。文章基于中国老年社会追踪调查（CLASS）数据，从空间可达性的视角，实证评估了老年友好社区建设对老年家庭消费的影响。研究发现，老年友好社区建设能够显著促进老年消费，优化老年消费结构，推动消费升级。机制分析表明，老年友好社区建设通过提升老年人健康感知、增加社会资本两条途径影响老年消费。异质性分析显示，低...

agingHealth.title: 经济与心理双视角下就业稳定性与青年女性生育意愿——兼论生育支持政策的调节作用
agingHealth.abstract: 文章基于2025年中国九省（市）青年女性婚育状况调查数据，从经济和心理双重视角研究就业稳定性对生育意愿的影响机制以及生育支持政策的调节作用。研究发现，不稳定就业和失业女性在未来两年内生育的可能性显著低于稳定就业女性。中介分析显示，不稳定就业和失业均会通过削弱女性的经济能力和养育信心降低其生育意愿，其中不稳定就业主要经由心理路径产生影响，而失业的经济与心理路径贡献相近。调节效应结果显示，经济补贴和带...

agingHealth.title: 灵活就业者的劳动供给选择——基于参考依赖偏好视角的研究发现
agingHealth.abstract: 相比于传统稳定就业群体，灵活就业者往往可以自由选择工作时间，然而调查数据显示他们面临更加严重的超时劳动问题。为理解这一现象及其背后的作用机制，文章基于参考依赖偏好理论分析了灵活就业者超时劳动的选择机制，并利用中国流动人口动态监测调查（CMDS）和中国社会状况综合调查（CSS）数据进行了实证检验。按照参考依赖偏好理论，当劳动者具有明确的收入参考标准时，工资率越低，越可能超时劳动。实证分析结果表明，参...

agingHealth.title: 职业空窗如何影响求职者重返劳动力市场——基于随机化简历实验的证据
agingHealth.abstract: 促进高质量充分就业，是新时代新征程就业工作的新定位、新使命。文章聚焦有工作经历的求职者考察其所经历的职业空窗对后续求职过程中企业雇佣决策的因果效应及边界条件。结合大规模在线招聘数据和随机化简历投递实验，文章实证分析显示，职业空窗对个人后续求职时企业的雇佣决策存在显著负向效应，且影响程度因职业中断原因而异：因考研或调休而辞职的负向效应较强，而因家庭原因中断职业的负向效应相对较弱；间隔时长本身的影响并...

agingHealth.title: 中国老年人照料缺口的规模、特征与趋势

agingHealth.abstract: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3263-3293 Abstract An increasing number of decisions are guided by machine learning algorithms. But when consequential decisions are encoded in algorithms, individuals may strategically alter their behavior to achieve desired outcomes. This paper develops an empirical approach that adjusts decision algorithms to anticipate manipulation. By explicitly modeling incentives to manipulate, our approach produces decision rules that are stable under manipulation, even when the rules are fully transparent. We use the expansion of the bus system in Jakarta, Indonesia, to study these trade-offs.
